newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to look deeper into ex-GE unit loss.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to look deeper into ex-GE unit loss.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Ministry on Monday urged the State Audit Office to investigate 1996 losses posted by Polgari Bank, which the state rebought in December from General Electric-controlled Budapest Bank.

The management appointed to run Polgari after GE bought Budapest Bank (BB) did not do enough to reduce risks created by the previous management, the ministry told reporters on publishing the results of its own investigation.

"We found that (Polgari) posted a serious loss," Deputy Secretary of State Agnes Balazs told a news conference. "We recommend a detailed investigation by a professional body, the Sytate Audit Office (ASZ)."

The state rebought Polgari from BB in December, fulfilling a state guarantee to General Electric Capital Services and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, who acquired a joint majority stake in BB in December 1995.

Polgari posted in 1996 a loss of some one billion forints on a balance sheet total of about 30 billion, the ministry said. Polgari lost its registered capital and it does not meet banking supervision capital requirements, Balazs said.
She said the Finance Ministry investigation had not unveiled what share of the responsibility the management appointed by new owners bore for Polgari's bad performance.

She added the ministry may initiate legal proceedings against those responsible for the losses once the ASZ have looked into the Polgari's transactions, which may have involved irregularities, with certain enterprises often mentioned in Polgari documents.
Opposition politicians have sharply criticised the government for buy back guarantees included in the sales contract with GE and EBRD.
